answers.answer: The draw deck is the 12 Speed cards, 3 Starting Upgrade cards, and 3 Stress cards shuffled together. Put the 6 Heat cards face up on the Engine, set the Gear pawn to 1st, and draw 7 cards.
answers.evidence: Setup: 'Shuffle your 12 Speed cards, 3 Starting Upgrade cards, and 3 Stress cards together as your draw deck'; 'Place 6 Heat cards face up on the Engine'; 'Set Gear pawn to 1st gear'; 'Draw 7 cards into your hand.'

answers.answer: Yes, you may stay in your current gear. You may shift two positions (for example, 1st to 3rd) by immediately paying 1 Heat during Shift Gears, moving it from Engine to discard. You must have that Heat available then; Heat in hand cannot pay.
answers.evidence: Shift Gears: 'Stay in your current gear'; two positions by 'immediately paying 1 Heat during this step'; Paying Heat: Engine to discard; Heat in hand cannot pay.

answers.answer: No. In 3rd gear you must play 3 cards if you have enough playable cards. Commit them face down.
answers.evidence: Play Cards: 'Play cards from hand face down equal to your gear number (… 3rd = 3).'

answers.answer: Steps 1 and 2 are simultaneous for all players, in that order. Everyone must finish both before step 3 begins. Then players take sequential turns frontmost car first, with each player completing steps 3–9 before the next player starts. Side-by-side, the car closer to the Race Line is ahead and goes first.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure and Sequential Phase: all complete 1 and 2 simultaneously; wait for everyone before step 3; each player completes 3–9 before the next; side-by-side car closest to Race Line is ahead for turn order.

answers.answer: Cars never block passage. If the destination space is full, place your car in the first free spot behind the blocking cars. If a spot in the destination is available, place the car on the spot closest to the Race Line.
answers.evidence: Blocked Movement: 'Cars never block passage'; full destination means 'first free spot behind the blocking cars.' Reveal & Move: place car on spot closest to Race Line if available.

answers.answer: Discard the flipped Heat and Starting Upgrade cards immediately, as they are non-Speed cards. The Speed 3 card goes into your Play Area on top of the played Stress card and supplies that Stress card's speed (3). The played Stress card remains underneath it in the Play Area and both are discarded at Replenish Hand. Resolve all played Stress before Adrenaline.
answers.evidence: Stress Cards: flip until a Speed appears; immediately discard each flipped non-Speed card, including Heat and Starting Upgrade; put found Speed on top of played Stress and use its value; Stress remains underneath; resolve all before Adrenaline.

answers.answer: In a five-car race, the last two cars to move receive Adrenaline, based on the number of cars that started. Each gets access to 1 extra Cooldown and may add 1 extra speed. The extra speed can be taken before or after Boost. Unused Adrenaline cannot be saved.
answers.evidence: Adrenaline: if race started with 5 or more cars, 'the last two cars to move' get benefits; 1 extra Cooldown and may add 1 extra speed; extra speed before or after Boost; unused Adrenaline cannot be saved.

answers.answer: Yes. In React you may use your 2nd-gear Cooldown allowance of 1 to move the Heat card from hand to Engine, then immediately spend it from Engine to Boost. Cooldown and Boost may be activated in any order; Cooldown specifically may be followed immediately by spending that Heat. Without first cooling it, Heat in hand cannot pay and an empty Engine cannot pay for Boost.
answers.evidence: React: activate Cooldown/Boost in any order; 'You may Cooldown Heat from your hand into your Engine, then immediately spend it to Boost.' Cooldown: 2nd gear provides 1; Paying Heat: hand Heat cannot pay; Boost requires Engine Heat.

answers.answer: You may Boost once per turn during React, paying 1 Heat from Engine to discard. If Engine is empty, you cannot Boost unless you first use available Cooldown to return Heat from hand to Engine. Flip and discard non-Speed cards until a Speed card appears; add it to your Play Area and move its value. Boost speed counts in total speed for corner checks.
answers.evidence: Boost: 'Once per turn during React,' pay 1 Heat from Engine; flip until Speed and add/move its value. Paying Heat: cannot Boost without Engine Heat; React allows Cooldown first. Corner check includes Boost speed.

answers.answer: Yes, Slipstream is optional. Corner speed is 6, excluding the two Slipstream spaces, so the limit-4 corner requires 2 Heat if you can pay.
answers.evidence: Slipstream: 'optionally move 2 spaces forward'; it 'does NOT increase your speed for corner checks.' Check Corner: pay Heat equal to speed excess; 6 minus 4 = 2.

answers.answer: Check both corners in the order crossed. Use speed 8 for each separate check: pay 2 for the limit-6 corner and 4 for the limit-4 corner, 6 Heat total.
answers.evidence: Check Corner: check every Corner Line crossed 'in the order crossed'; for each separately use the same total speed; pay excess. Here excesses are 8−6=2 and 8−4=4.

answers.answer: The limit-4 corner costs 3 Heat at speed 7, but you can pay only 2, so you spin out. Discard all remaining Engine Heat, move back to the first available space before that corner, take 2 Stress cards directly into your hand (because you were in 4th gear), and set your gear to 1st.
answers.evidence: Spin Out: if unable to pay enough, move all remaining Engine Heat to discard and return to first available space before the corner; take 2 Stress into hand in 3rd/4th gear; move Gear pawn to 1st.

answers.answer: You may discard unwanted Speed cards, but not Stress or Heat cards. You may not browse any discard pile, including your own; only the top card of each pile is public knowledge.
answers.evidence: Discard: may discard unwanted hand cards but 'never Stress or Heat'; nobody may browse any discard pile; only the top card is public knowledge.

answers.answer: Move all Play Area cards to your discard pile, then draw only enough cards to bring your hand back to 7, not seven additional cards.
answers.evidence: Replenish Hand: 'Move all Play Area cards to your discard pile, then draw only enough cards to bring your hand back to 7.'

answers.answer: Shuffle your discard pile into a new draw deck and continue the interrupted flips. Do not include cards still in your Play Area; they have not yet been discarded.
answers.evidence: Running Out of Cards: when draw deck is empty, shuffle discard into a new draw deck and continue interrupted draws/flips; do not include cards still in Play Area.

answers.answer: When paying Heat, move it from Engine to discard. It can cycle from discard to draw deck to hand and returns to Engine only via Cooldown. Heat cannot normally be played or voluntarily discarded from hand.
answers.evidence: Paying Heat: Engine to discard. Heat Card Cycle: 'Engine to discard to draw deck to hand; only returns to Engine via Cooldown.' Heat cannot normally be played or voluntarily discarded from hand.

answers.answer: Commit the 2 playable cards and fill the two remaining required slots with Heat cards in the Play Area. Your car moves zero spaces. Set your gear to 1st, discard all committed cards including the covering Heat, and skip directly to Replenish Hand. You skip React, so cannot Cooldown or Boost this turn.
answers.evidence: Cluttered Hand: commit all playable cards and fill remaining slots with Heat; car moves zero; set gear to 1st; discard committed cards including covering Heat; skip to step 9 and skip React.

answers.answer: The first to cross during the round does not automatically win. If multiple cars finish in the same round, the car furthest ahead wins, with the Race Line breaking a tie. At round end remove all cars that crossed the final finish line and place them in finishing order on the Hall of Fame.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: multiple cars finishing in same round are ranked by furthest ahead, closest to Race Line breaks ties; at end of round remove finishers and place in order on Hall of Fame.

answers.answer: On the final lap, you cannot Slipstream across the finish line or Slipstream after crossing it. After crossing the final finish line, ignore speed limits of corners beyond it and move as far as you can.
answers.evidence: Scoring: final-lap Slipstream cannot cross the finish or happen after crossing; after crossing final finish, ignore corner speed limits beyond it.

answers.answer: Both remaining cars receive Adrenaline, because the race started with six cars. Eligibility uses the starting car count even after finishers leave the track; with 5 or more starters the last two cars to move receive it.
answers.evidence: Adrenaline: use number of cars that started even after finishers leave; if race started with 5 or more, last two cars to move receive benefits.

answers.answer: Use the lap count printed on the selected board. The USA track normally uses 2 laps; for a first USA learning race, you may race 1 lap instead.
answers.evidence: Setup: 'Use the number of laps printed on the selected board'; first USA learning race may be 1 lap instead of its normal 2.

answers.answer: Do not assume every track always uses 6 Heat and 3 Stress. Check the board for how many of each each player adds; the summary says the typical count is 6 Heat and 3 Stress.
answers.evidence: Setup: 'Check the board for how many Heat and Stress cards each player adds (typically 6 Heat and 3 Stress).'

answers.answer: Randomly place all cars on the starting grid in ascending order. The summary does not explicitly say whether players may choose preferred positions, though it specifies random placement rather than player selection.
answers.evidence: Setup: 'Randomly place all cars on the starting grid in ascending order.' Sequential Phase establishes turn order as frontmost car first; side-by-side, closest to Race Line is ahead.

answers.answer: Place the remaining Stress cards face up near the board as a reserve.
answers.evidence: Setup: 'Place the remaining Stress cards face up near the board as a reserve.'

answers.answer: Unsupported: the supplied summary does not describe an optional setup handicap for an experienced driver racing beginners or any addition/removal of Heat for a particular car.
answers.evidence: The Setup section gives standard components, Heat/Stress counts, and starting hand; no experienced-driver handicap is stated.

answers.answer: No. The largest shift is two positions, such as 1st to 3rd, and it costs 1 Heat paid immediately during Shift Gears from Engine to discard.
answers.evidence: Shift Gears permits shifting two positions by immediately paying 1 Heat; Player Reference gives examples 1st to 3rd and 2nd to 4th.

answers.answer: No. A two-position shift must be paid immediately during Shift Gears, from Heat available in Engine. Heat in hand cannot pay; later React Cooldown cannot retroactively pay the shift cost.
answers.evidence: Shift Gears: pay immediately during this step and must have Heat available; Paying Heat: hand Heat cannot pay. React occurs later (step 5).

answers.answer: Each played Stress card is resolved by flipping until its own Speed card appears. The found Speed 3 and Speed 4 cards supply the two Stress cards' speed, so total speed is 2+3+4=9. They are added from the draw-deck flip resolution, not committed from hand; the hand commitment was the two Stress cards and Speed 2.
answers.evidence: Stress Cards: 'For each Stress card you played, flip cards ... until a Speed card appears'; found Speed is put in Play Area on top of the played Stress and supplies its speed.

answers.answer: Unsupported: the summary says to move forward the total speed and explains the forced stop when a destination space is full, but does not say whether a player may voluntarily move fewer spaces to avoid a corner.
answers.evidence: Reveal & Move says sum values and move forward that many spaces; Blocked Movement only describes a full destination. No voluntary stopping rule is stated.

answers.answer: Use total speed 8, not the 5 spaces actually moved. The corner check uses the same total speed for the round; at limit 6, pay 2 Heat if able.
answers.evidence: Check Corner: compare 'your total speed for the round' with the limit, using the same total speed for each corner; excess is paid. 8−6=2.

answers.answer: No. A corner is checked only if you crossed its Corner Line; being near it without crossing does not incur a check or Heat payment.
answers.evidence: Check Corner: 'Check every Corner Line crossed this turn'; step 7 applies if crossed a Corner Line.

answers.answer: At speed 6 or below the limit-6 corner, you pay nothing, so an empty Engine alone does not cause a spin out. A spin out occurs when a required Heat cost cannot be paid.
answers.evidence: Check Corner: if speed does not exceed limit, pay nothing. Spin Out: occurs if you cannot pay enough Heat for a corner.

answers.answer: You successfully pay the 3 Heat and continue; the summary says to spin out only if you cannot pay enough. It does not require retaining Heat in Engine after payment.
answers.evidence: Paying Heat moves the required cards from Engine to discard; Spin Out applies if you 'cannot pay enough Heat.'

answers.answer: Pay 2 Heat at the limit-6 corner, leaving 3. The limit-4 corner then requires 4, which you cannot fully pay, so that second corner causes the spin out. Move the remaining 3 Heat to discard and return to the first available space before the second corner. Take 2 Stress cards into hand for 4th gear and set gear to 1st.
answers.evidence: Check Corner uses the same speed for each corner and charges excess separately. Spin Out moves all remaining Engine Heat to discard, returns before the corner causing spin out, gives 2 Stress into hand in 3rd/4th gear, and sets 1st gear.

answers.answer: Take 1 extra Stress card directly into your hand and end in 1st gear.
answers.evidence: Spin Out: 1 Stress into hand in 1st/2nd gear; then move Gear pawn to 1st.

answers.answer: 1st gear provides Cooldown 3. With Adrenaline's extra Cooldown, the maximum available is 4. You are not forced to use all of it: Cooldown is activated if chosen, and it moves Heat from hand to Engine.
answers.evidence: Player Reference: 1st gear Cooldown 3. Adrenaline grants access to 1 extra Cooldown. React says activate available Cooldown; Cooldown says move Heat from hand to Engine.

answers.answer: Yes. Adrenaline's extra speed is something you 'may' add, while the Cooldown and Boost symbols may be activated in any order; the summary does not make taking the extra speed a condition for using extra Cooldown.
answers.evidence: Adrenaline: 'gains access to 1 extra Cooldown and may add 1 extra speed'; React: activate available Cooldown and/or Boost in any order.

answers.answer: Yes. Adrenaline eligibility is for the last car(s) to move, so overtaking during your move does not change that eligibility. With four cars that started, only the last car receives it; the second-to-last also qualifies only when the race started with 5 or more cars.
answers.evidence: Adrenaline: last car to move gets benefits; last two only if race started with 5 or more cars. Sequential turns proceed from frontmost to last.

answers.answer: You qualify if you end next to another car or in the space immediately behind a car. If neither, you do not qualify.
answers.evidence: Slipstream: 'If you end next to another car or in the space immediately behind a car' you may move 2 spaces.

answers.answer: Yes, if your position after Boost at the later Slipstream step is immediately behind a car. React (including Boost) comes before Slipstream, and eligibility is described by where you end for Slipstream; the summary does not say eligibility is locked at Reveal & Move.
answers.evidence: Turn sequence puts React before Slipstream; Slipstream condition is 'If you end next to another car or in the space immediately behind a car.'

answers.answer: Just one optional two-space Slipstream move; the summary describes one move when you satisfy the positional condition, not one move per nearby car.
answers.evidence: Slipstream: if you end next to another car or immediately behind a car, 'optionally move 2 spaces forward.'

answers.answer: The occupied destination does not permit sharing: if a destination space is full, use the first free spot behind the blocking cars. Corner-check speed does not include Slipstream movement, even if Slipstream crosses a Corner Line; the corner still must be checked using total speed excluding Slipstream. The summary does not specify a special reduction to the 2-space Slipstream move if its destination is full.
answers.evidence: Blocked Movement: if destination is full, place car in first free spot behind blocking cars. Slipstream: movement does not increase speed for corner checks, but crossing a Corner Line still requires checking.

answers.answer: No. Check the limit-4 corner before the finish line: at speed 8 it costs 4 Heat. Ignore the limit-3 corner beyond the final finish line, so total Heat due is 4.
answers.evidence: Check Corner: check crossed Corner Lines and pay excess. Final-lap rule says after crossing final finish, ignore speed limits of corners beyond it. 8−4=4.

answers.answer: The summary bars Slipstream across the finish line on the final lap, implying this restriction does not apply at the end of a non-final lap; however, it does not explicitly state non-final finish-line Slipstream permission. Corners beyond a final finish line are ignored only after crossing that final finish line; the summary does not specifically discuss corners beyond a non-final lap's start/finish line.
answers.evidence: Slipstream states 'On the final lap' you cannot cross the finish; final-lap scoring says ignore corners beyond the final finish line. No non-final-lap corner instruction is explicit.

answers.answer: Other cars continue racing. At the end of each round, cars that crossed the final finish line are removed and placed in finishing order; continue until all cars finish.
answers.evidence: Scoring: remove finishers at end of round, then 'Continue playing until all cars finish.'

answers.answer: Unsupported: the summary does not mention a Legends Line or explain whether crossing it triggers a payment or when it is used. It identifies Corner Lines as the lines checked for Heat payment.
answers.evidence: Check Corner describes checking every Corner Line crossed; no Legends Line is mentioned in the summary.

answers.answer: No. You shift first, then commit cards equal to the new gear. After shifting down from 3rd to 2nd, two playable cards fill the two required slots, so Cluttered Hand does not apply.
answers.evidence: Simultaneous Phase: Shift Gears then Play Cards; Play Cards equals gear number. Cluttered Hand applies when Heat leaves too few playable cards for your gear.
